data.title: Documented: Custody Logs
data.description:
Documented is a private record of how you show up for your kids.

Log what happened (a handoff, a missed exchange, a first sentence, a doctor's visit) and it is sealed the second you save it. Time captured automatically. Place attached if you want it. Nothing you can quietly rewrite later, which is exactly what makes it worth something.

WHY SEALED MATTERS

A note you typed months after the fact is a memory. A record made at the time is a different thing.

Every entry gets a SHA-256 fingerprint linked to the entry before it. Change one character and the chain no longer matches, and the app tells you. Edits can't be hidden. That's what tamper-evident means.

Separately, each entry's fingerprint is sent to an independent Time-Stamping Authority, which signs a statement that it existed at that moment. The stamp is requested the moment the entry seals, and if your phone is offline it's obtained as soon as you reconnect. Only the fingerprint leaves your phone, never your words, your photos, your children's names, or where you were. A fingerprint can't be turned back into your content.

BUILT FOR HOW THIS ACTUALLY HAPPENS

Thirty seconds, one-handed, in a car park, before you forget. Write it, tag it, seal it.

• Log notes, photos, videos, voice memos, receipts, and message screenshots
• Tag which child, and which co-parent, each moment involved
• Automatic timestamp and optional GPS, captured rather than typed
• Corrections are amendments: the original stays, the correction sits beside it
• Search and filter by child, category, or date

PRIVATE BY DEFAULT

No account. No sign-up. No password. Documented opens straight into your record.

Your entries stay on your iPhone, and in your own iCloud storage if you turn sync on. We can't read them. Your co-parent is never contacted, never notified, and never given access. Naming someone in your record is a label on your record, nothing more.

WHAT IT COSTS

Documented is a subscription, with a 7-day free trial. The subscription is the app, not an add-on to it.

Included, with no limits of any kind: writing new entries, sealing them, the independent timestamp, photos, videos, voice memos and receipts, iCloud sync of your own record, search, filtering, amendments, the PDF export, and encrypted sharing with your attorney. No entry limit. No attachment limit. No storage tier.

Free, whether you subscribe or not: reading, searching and verifying everything already in your record. Nothing you have sealed is ever locked away from you, and if a trial ends without a purchase the record becomes read-only rather than closed.

People who installed Documented before this change keep their original free terms permanently.

WHEN YOU NEED TO PRODUCE IT

Your whole record becomes one PDF, ready to hand to your attorney: every entry in order, with its seal, an integrity statement, and your attachments. Any single entry can go on its own. You can send that record to your attorney encrypted on your device, to a key only they hold.

A NOTE ON WHAT THIS IS

Documented is a record-keeping tool. We're not a law firm and we don't give legal advice. Whether any record is accepted is decided by a judge under the rules of evidence where you live. What we can do is make sure that when you wrote something down, it's provable that you wrote it down then, and that nobody, including you, quietly changed it since.

If something is on the line, talk to a licensed attorney in your state.

data.release_notes:
Your imported texts are now locked as they arrived.

Once a Messages conversation is in your record, no one can edit, correct or reword it, and that includes you. The texts are sealed exactly as your phone had them. You can still name the other person in the thread, because that changes no message.

ALSO IN THIS UPDATE
Long imported conversations are easier to read. They show as a short preview card on the timeline, open on the message your search found, and display the date and time of each text. They are sealed as pages of 20 messages, not one long strip, and a PDF export prints them the same way.

Every attached photo and video now shows the date it was captured. One tap makes that date the entry's event date.

Photos open in a gallery you can swipe through. Swipe down to close a photo or video, and a pinch to zoom no longer closes it by mistake.

When you attach several photos, Documented waits for all of them before sealing. If one can't be loaded, it tells you which one, so it isn't quietly left out.

If a change can't be saved, the app now says so instead of failing silently. Edits made while iCloud is unavailable are saved on your phone and synced once it's back.

If you use Documented on two iPhones, your evidence library now combines changes from both, with no duplicates and nothing lost.

If you cancel your subscription, a final screen tells you when your access ends, confirms you won't be charged again, and reminds you that your record stays readable.

Fixes for the plans screen at large text sizes and on smaller iPhones.
